findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to present the company’s Exclusion and Restriction policy to the inspector. The PIC stated they would send the policy to the inspector, but this did not happen within 24 hours of the investigation, despite a follow up phone call from the inspector. The inspector provided a blank copy of SCDPH’s Employee Health Reporting Agreement to the PIC. Inspector will return on 03/24 to ensure that the PIC has EITHER obtained signed copies of SCDPH’s employee health reporting agreements from employees, OR can show the inspector the company’s exclusion/ restriction policy. All food establishments must have a verifiable manner to confirm reportable illnesses.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed sanitizer buckets throughout the kitchen holding below the concentration required for food contact surfaces (100 ppm quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- sanitizer buckets were remade to proper concentration. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the appropriate concentration for food contact surfaces per the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facilities in need of repair or maintenance:
1) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall is peeling.
2) The floor drain below the drive thru register is missing a floor drain cover.
3) There is no outlet cover on the wall behind the ice cream machine.
4) THIRD REPEAT: There is a missing floor tile in front of the back door. 
Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the entry and microorganisms with high water activity. Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) FIRST REPEAT: There is an accumulation of grease in the hood vent above the fryers. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination on ready to eat (RTE) foods, and also pose a fire risk to the facility. 
2) Food and general debris on the wall and floor beneath the front counter.
3) Dust on the wall behind the drive thru drink machine.
Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed a broken floor tile in front of the back door. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure tiles are repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Scrambled egg cartons in the chest cooler (near the make lines) were observed at 56F (probed). CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Foods recently prepped (tomatoes) or recently placed in the cooler (sliced cheese) were moved to the walk-in cooler. Ensure foods are held at 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The chest cooler near the make lines is not functioning properly to hold foods at 41F or below. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Foods recently placed in the cooler were moved to the walk-in cooler for storage. Make the necessary repairs so the cooler holds foods at 41F or below.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Ambient thermometers were not found in the chest cooler near the make lines or in the walk-in cooler. Ensure all cold holding units have ambient thermometers present inside to monitor the air temperature.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Several broken wall and floor tiles observed around the back door. Repair broken tiles so wall and floor is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Employee was observed handling French fry boxes for orders along the top edge and inner surface where fries have the potential to touch. Ensure employees prevent bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in  (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Hood filters over fryers were soiled with grease buildup. PIC noted filters were scheduled to be cleaned this Sunday (every two weeks).
Clean the aforementioned items and all nonfood contact surfaces as needed and maintain them clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris. [C]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Murky water observed ponding in the corner near the 3 compartment sink. Ensure wastewater is properly removed from the facility. Eliminate ponding water.
5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulking around mop sink is separated from the basin, with soil accumulation around it. Clean and recaulk mop sink.
2) Several broken wall and floor tiles observed around the back door. Repair broken tiles so wall and floor is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employees were observed adjusting face masks and then continuing to the next task without washing hands. Handwashing was discussed. Ensure staff are washing hands between tasks, including after they touch/adjust face masks. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Employee preparing beverages at the drive thru was observed scooping ice with cups instead of the designated ice scoop. Employee was advised on proper use of the ice scoop for dispensing ice. 
Employee was later observed handling French fry boxes for orders along the top edge and inner surface where fries have the potential to touch. PIC was advised of observation and spoke with employee about proper handling of fry boxes to avoid bare hand contact with food.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was not posted in the men’s restroom. Provide a handwashing sign in the men’s restroom.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1. Pink and black mold buildup was observed along the bottom surface of the white baffle in the ice machine. Condensation was dripping off the surfaces where mold was observed. PIC cleaned the baffle during the inspection and discarded a portion of the ice after cleaning. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
2. Pan for ice scoop storage on the right ledge of the ice machine was soiled with general buildup in the bottom. The pan was also position directly in front of the side vent where air blows out from the condensing unit. Ice scoop and holder were cleaned and sanitized during inspection, and proper storage in a clean protected location was discussed. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer solutions were observed at 100ppm and some solutions were murky from use. Solutions were discarded and fresh sanitizer was provided at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed as needed throughout daily operations and maintained at proper concentration. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Clean equipment was soiled with flour buildup in a plastic tub stored on a rack to the left of the chicken breading station. Ensure clean equipment is stored so it is protected prior to using. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 One of the hood filters above the fryers had a screen that was in disrepair and pulling apart. Replace the damaged hood filter. 
Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 (B) Clean pans available for use at the chicken breading station were soiled with stuck on food debris. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing prior to storing equipment for use in staging areas. Repeat wash, rinse, and sanitize process as many times as needed in addition to pre-soaking and scrubbing to ensure food debris is removed. 
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1. Detail cleaning is needed for general surfaces of equipment, such as lower shelves, brackets, and legs/wheels. 
2. Unused cooler on the right side of the fryers was soiled inside with buildup along the ledge beneath the condensing unit and condensation in the bottom.
3. Hood filters over fryers were soiled with grease buildup. PIC noted filters were scheduled to be cleaned this evening.
Clean the aforementioned items and all nonfood contact surfaces as needed and maintain them clean.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Two sani-buckets were observed at 0ppm quat. Solutions were discarded and fresh sanitizer solution was provided at proper concentration of 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed as needed throughout daily operations and maintained at proper concentration. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold buildup was starting to occur on surfaces of the white baffle in the ice machine. Cleaning and sanitizing frequency were discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Backup pan of cheese slices on the make line had two stickers for a time stamp. One sticker was not marked with the time, and the other sticker was marked with a time of 2pm. It was already after 3pm, and all other time stamps were marked for 6pm. Management confirmed the discard time is to be marked on the stickers used for tracking time control, and it would appear someone marked the time product was removed from the cooler instead of time of discard. Benefit of the doubt was given and cheese was kept for use. A time stamp was placed on the container with 6pm discard time. Ensure that all staff are properly marking time for working supplies of foods on the make line.  
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. The food must be served or discarded within 4 hours.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Light was visible at the bottom left corner of the back door where door sweep was in disrepair. PIC stated a work order would be placed for repairs.
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Pan for ice scoop storage at the ice machine was soiled with general buildup in the bottom. A clean pan was provided for storage of ice scoop. Cleaning frequency was discussed for ice scoop and storage pan.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in clean, protected location if utensils, such as ice scoops, are used w/ non-TCS food.

4-202.16 One of the hood filters above the fryers had a screen that was in disrepair and pulling apart. Replace the damaged hood filter. 
Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

1. storage cabinet at icee machine (sticky buildup of syrup);
2. metal table holding vegetable slicer (food debris/general buildup);  and
3. hood filters (grease buildup).
Clean the aforementioned items and all nonfood contact surfaces as needed and maintain them clean.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor under ice machine and along the wall behind the ice machine was soiled with buildup of general debris. The floor drain by the ice machine was also soiled with chunky mold buildup. Clean the floor and the drain at the ice machine. Clean the floors throughout under equipment and floor drains as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.113 Wet mop was stored in the mop bucket by the back door. Properly store wet mops between uses, and ensure proper disposal of all waste water from the buckets.
Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be stored so they are not a source of contamination for food and food related items and in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11  Handsink in women's room was pulling away from the wall where caulk was in disrepair. Handsink in men's room had gaps in the caulk where it was sealed to the wall.
Reseal the handsinks to the wall in both restrooms.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.
